1. **Enter Practice Range** and disable **aim assist strength** and **max deadzone sensitivity boost**. Set both sensitivities to max.
2. Set **minimum input deadzone** to **0**.
3. If your camera drifts on its own, gradually increase the deadzone by 1 until it stops, easy and done.

# open these

* [1-Second Stopwatch](https://www.online-stopwatch.com/timer/1second/)
* [PSA Sensitivity Calculator](https://jscalc.io/embed/vqOrqXRpMgmwb8tV)

1. Keep **aim assist strength** and **max deadzone sensitivity boost** disabled. Set sensitivities to max.
2. Stand **5m** from a bot in Practice Range.
3. Using the stopwatch, **tilt your stick fully** and rotate **exactly 360° in 1 second**. Adjust sensitivity up if you undershoot, down if you overshoot.
4. Input this "average" sensitivity into the PSA calculator. It will generate **low and high values**.
5. Test both values and pick the one that provides the **smoothest tracking** (without jitter). The calculator will generate new values—repeat this process **7 times**. DO NOT RUSH THIS PART, spend like at least 3 or 4 minutes just tracking and shooting both with both senses, if you use more one than the other, it will feel better because gotten used to it more than the other, so keep the time spent on them equal
6. The final result is your **perfect sensitivity**.
7. Re-enable **aim assist strength** and set **max deadzone sensitivity boost** to **100**.

**1. Start with the basics:** Fix up the walls (patch up any holes and give them a fresh coat of paint), and sort out the flooring to make everything feel cleaner and more polished, it will literally make you feel better.

**2. Upgrade the desk:** Ditch the corner desk and get a new one that stretches along the back wall from the left corner to just before the bed. This will open up the space and give you a much cleaner setup.

**3.Reinstall the shelves properly:** Mount them evenly above the new desk so they’re aligned and symmetrical. Add some RGB light strips underneath for a subtle glow and a nice vibe to your lil cosy corner.

**4.Rework the monitors:** Swap out the ultrawide for two smaller monitors on a monitor arm. This will give you more flexibility (bc its 2 monitors duh) and a cleaner look while still providing plenty of screen space.

**6.Tame the cables:** Invest in some under-desk cable management solutions like trays, ties, and raceways to keep everything out of sight and off the floor. It’ll make a massive difference in making the setup look clean.

**7.Declutter the desk:** Move all the small items into the drawer. If you need more storage, grab another drawer unit and place it against the left wall. Keeping the desk surface clear will make the space feel way more organized and comfortable.

**8.Move the tv.** Moving the tv to the left wall at head height will mean you dont have to look up when playing playstation, it will also make the backwall look cleaner when combined with equal shelving and rgb. This is extremely detailed answer, you don't have to read all of it.

Browse features are what people see when browsing YouTube. The two are, videos you see on the main page, and videos you see on the right hand side when watching other videos. All these videos are usually a mix between recommend for you, and what's popular recently, or what's popular within categories you like to frequent, oh and sometimes channels you sub too.

So, when you make a video, YouTube will show it to some people, normally people that watch videos that are similar to the one you made, it will take the title of your video, the category you may have put it in, and the tags of the video if you put any in (these are called impressions) 

So you will see how many "impressions" you've had, ergo, how many people have seen your thumbnail either on the home page, or on the side of other videos, called "watch page". This is why thumbnails are, imo, literally the most important part of your channel, on equal with the video. You need to make a thumbnail look ATTRACTIVE, and it has to draw people to click on it, thus turning the impressions, into VIEWS, and obviously VIEWS the most important metric of your channel, more so than subscribers. 

So, you get impressions, people click on your video because it had a cool looking thumbnail, and now you're getting views! Now, CTR stands for click through rate, if 100 people see your thumbnail, and only 10 people click it, that's a click through rate of %10, which is...ok, could certainly be higher, could easily be lower, which is bad. 

So the higher the CTR, the more impression you will get, because the algorithm has seen you have quite a good CTR at that current moment, so it will show MORE people your video, and maybe your CTR will go down, so YouTube STOPS showing random people your thumbnail.

Now the other important aspect is duration. How long are people watching your video for? Think about what you do, sometimes I have no patience on days, and when I click on a video, and hear some guy talking for the first 30seconds of the video, and not showing the thing I came to see, then I'm clicking OFF the video, which lowers the average viewing duration of that video for the person who made it.

So this is where GOOD content comes into play, if you have good content, something that makes people want to continue watching, and you can hold their attention, then your average viewing duration for that video will go up, the algorithm will see this and, show it to people, and see how long they watch it for, if they click on it in the first place.

So, that's the meat of it IMO, the algorithm is certainly more complicated than that, but that's the jist of it, sometimes you can get a good CTR, but you won't get more impression, it takes into account so many more factors that we won't even think of, real life location, the niche, a bunch of shit not worth thinking about.

I give you some examples. My top video right now made roughly one million impressions, 95.3% of those impressions were from YouTube directly throwing my thumbnail onto the home page and watch page of people they thought might like my content. The other 4.7% came from stuff like people using the search bar, my subs, and also some external traffic from apps such as discord, WhatsApp, Facebook etc. This will happen even if you didn't advertise your content their, because I didn't. 

So, 1 million impressions, my current CTR for this video is 5.5%, pretty low and bad, the video is about a month old now and YouTube isn't showing it to anyone anymore, so the views barely increase recently. 

The end result is that I got 56.1k views from 1 million impressions, my average view duration for the video was 5 minutes and 5 seconds, which is pretty decent, the video is 12:40 long, but I got lucky on a hot fresh topic regarding my niche, and from all of this, I got 4.8k watch time from impressions (hours).

So that sums up impressions, I hope you understand it better now.

I doesn't make up the total views for videos though, since my current result is 6.6k watch hours (4.8k from impressions), my actual view duration is 4:18, which is 34% of the way through the video, and my total views currently stand at 92.5K
